description: Tune the Workflow section: slow down animations to a cinematic pace, enlarge cards with bigger fonts/icons/padding, and spread cards across the full canvas width. Use the /frontend-design skill for all UI implementation to ensure high design quality.
agentInstructions: IMPORTANT: For every story that modifies UI components (WorkflowNode.tsx, Workflow.tsx, or any visual changes), you MUST use the /frontend-design skill by invoking it before writing code. This skill generates distinctive, production-grade frontend code with high design quality. Invoke it by calling the Skill tool with skill='frontend-design' and pass the component requirements as args. The skill will help you produce polished, visually refined output rather than generic-looking code. DESIGN COHERENCE: The workflow component must feel coherent with the overall website style — use the existing design tokens (forest/coral/cream palette), font-display for headings, font-body for text, Tailwind utility classes, and the same visual language as other sections on the site. The cards should feel like a natural part of the B2B Sport website, not a separate widget.

userStories.title: Slow down animation timing to cinematic pace
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow animation to feel leisurely and cinematic rather than rushed, so I can comfortably read each step as it appears.
acceptanceCriteria: IMPORTANT: Use the /frontend-design skill before implementing CSS animation changes

FIX EDGE REVEAL SEQUENCE: Currently edges appear simultaneously with the target node. Instead, edges must draw in BETWEEN node reveals. The animation sequence for each pair must be: Node N appears (1500ms fade+scale) → pause → Edge from N to N+1 draws in (800ms) → pause → Node N+1 appears. This requires separate state tracking for visible edges vs visible nodes.
Add a new state variable visibleEdgeIndex (separate from visibleStepIndex) to control edge visibility independently from node visibility
Update stepsToEdges to use visibleEdgeIndex instead of visibleUpTo for the edge visibility condition

In the startAnimation callback, schedule edges as distinct phases between nodes. Example sequence for each step i>0: first reveal node i, then after a pause (e.g. 800ms), reveal the edge from node i to node i+1, then after another pause (e.g. 700ms), reveal node i+1
In the <style> block in Workflow.tsx: change node transition duration from 400ms to 1500ms for both opacity and transform
Change edge stroke-dashoffset transition from 300ms to 800ms
Change @keyframes workflowPulse animation — slow each cycle to 1.2s instead of 0.6s
Per-step timing should be approximately: 1500ms node reveal + 800ms pause + 800ms edge draw + 700ms pause = ~3800ms per step
Change initial delay before first node from 200ms to 500ms
Change pulse duration on non-last nodes from 600ms to 2000ms before clearing activeStepIndex
Change pulse duration on last node from 1800ms to 3000ms
Change hold time after all nodes revealed from 2500ms to 4000ms
Change fade-out + pause restart delay from 500ms to 1000ms
Add a CSS transition for fade-out: the workflow-node-hidden class should also use 800ms transition (not 400ms) so the fade-out is slow too — edges should also fade out slowly with 800ms transition
Total cycle for 6 nodes should be approximately 28-32 seconds with the edge phases included
Typecheck passes

Visual verification: Navigate to /en, scroll to workflow section, confirm the sequence is: node appears → edge draws to next position → next node appears → edge draws → etc. Edges should NOT appear simultaneously with nodes.
userStories.notes: CRITICAL: The current bug is that stepsToEdges uses the same visibleUpTo as nodes, causing edges to appear at the same time as their target node. You need a separate visibleEdgeIndex state and separate setTimeout entries in the animation loop for edges. The sequence per step is: Node fade-in (1500ms) → pulse on node → edge draw-in (800ms) → next node fade-in. Update both CSS transition durations AND JavaScript setTimeout values — they must be in sync.

userStories.title: Enlarge workflow node cards with bigger fonts and icons
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow cards to feel substantial and premium with large, easily readable text and prominent icons.
acceptanceCriteria: IMPORTANT: Use the /frontend-design skill before implementing the card redesign — pass it the current WorkflowNode.tsx and MobileWorkflowStep code and ask for a polished, larger card design
In WorkflowNode.tsx: increase icon container from w-10 h-10 to w-14 h-14 with rounded-xl
Increase icon SVG size from w-5 h-5 to w-7 h-7
Increase label text from text-sm to text-lg and make it font-bold (much bigger and prominent)
Increase description text from text-xs to text-base for easy readability
Increase stat text from text-xs to text-base
Increase card padding from px-4 py-3 to px-6 py-5 for generous breathing room
Increase gap between icon and text content from gap-3 to gap-4
Increase node min-width from min-w-[200px] to min-w-[260px]

In MobileWorkflowStep in Workflow.tsx: increase icon to w-12 h-12, label to text-base font-bold, description to text-sm, stat to text-sm, padding to px-5 py-4, max-width from max-w-[200px] to max-w-[280px]
Cards should feel substantial, premium, and easy to read at a glance — not cramped
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm workflow cards are noticeably larger with bigger icons and prominent text
userStories.notes: Use the /frontend-design skill to ensure the enlarged cards have refined visual design — good spacing ratios, visual hierarchy between label/description/stat, and a polished feel. The cards should look intentionally designed, not just scaled up.

userStories.title: Spread cards across full canvas width with generous gaps
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow cards spread across the full available width with generous breathing room between them, not clustered together.
acceptanceCriteria: IMPORTANT: Use the /frontend-design skill before implementing layout changes
Update scatteredPositions6 array to spread across a wider X range: approximately [{x:0,y:80}, {x:280,y:0}, {x:560,y:130}, {x:880,y:20}, {x:1160,y:140}, {x:1440,y:50}] — spanning 0 to ~1440px
Maintain varied horizontal gaps (some slightly wider, some slightly narrower) for organic feel
Y positions spread more vertically: use range 0-140 instead of current 0-110
Update getScatteredPositions function for dynamic generation: increase baseGap to 320 for <=4 steps, 280 for <=6 steps, 220 for >6 steps
Increase canvas height from h-[340px] to h-[420px] to give larger cards more vertical breathing room
Increase fitView padding from 0.2 to 0.35 to ensure cards have margin from canvas edges
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm workflow cards are spread across the full width with generous gaps — no clustering in the center
userStories.notes: Use the /frontend-design skill to ensure the overall layout composition feels balanced and intentional. The spacing should create a pleasant visual rhythm across the full width.
